tur75-10: According to a Cochrane review, exercise slightly improves hand pain, function and finger stiffness, with an average reduction in pain of half a point on a 0–10 scale. The effect is small and the quality of the evidence is low, but side effects are few and mild. Done regularly, it is a low-side-effect way to keep your hands moving. The recommendations of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) likewise advise considering hand exercises for every patient, along with training in joint-protecting use and assistive devices; the effect of exercise is small and fades when it is stopped. In osteoarthritis at the base of the thumb, a splint worn long-term, for at least 3 months, can ease pain.
